docs.title: Flash-Excel
docs.text: Flash-Excel is a Windows desktop application that cleans and reshapes Excel and CSV files with reusable presets: you describe the transformation once, then apply it to any number of files, by hand or on a schedule.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick start
docs.text: New to Flash-Excel? Get started takes you from the installer to your first transformed file in a few minutes.

docs.title: Does Flash-Excel change my source file?
docs.text: No. Every run writes a new output file, by default Documents\flash-excel\output\<name>_clean.<extension>, and leaves the source as it is. The one exception is a naming pattern of {name} with the source's own folder and format: the output then replaces the source. See File formats.

docs.title: Does Flash-Excel run on macOS or Linux?
docs.text: No. Flash-Excel is a Windows application: its installer, its settings and its scheduling all rely on Windows.

docs.title: Do I need administrator rights?
docs.text: No. Flash-Excel installs for your Windows user only, and updates install the same way. See Get started.

docs.title: Are my files sent anywhere?
docs.text: No. Files are read, transformed and written on your PC. The only network access is the check for a new version when Flash-Excel starts, and the download of an update when you select it. See Automatic updates.

docs.title: Which files can Flash-Excel read and write?
docs.text: It reads .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls and .csv files, and writes .xlsx, .csv and .parquet files. See File formats.

docs.title: Can I process another sheet than the first one?
docs.text: No. Flash-Excel reads the first sheet of a workbook only. Move the sheet you need to the first position in Excel, save, and run again.

docs.title: Can I process several files at once?
docs.text: Yes. Select or drop several files on the Processing page: they are processed one after the other with the same preset, each into its own output file. See Run a preset.

docs.title: Is there a size limit for files?
docs.text: There is no fixed limit. Each file is read entirely into memory, so very large files need enough free memory on your PC.

docs.title: Can I try a preset without writing a file?
docs.text: Yes. Preview on the Processing page shows the result on the first 100 rows, without writing anything. See Preview a transformation.

docs.title: Can I change the order of the steps?
docs.text: Not in the editor: it runs the configured steps in a fixed order designed so each step finds the columns it needs. A preset file written by hand runs its steps in the order of the file. See Steps and their order.

docs.title: Why are the computed column functions in French?
docs.text: They follow the function names of the French version of Excel (SI, CONCATENER, ARRONDI…). They stay the same in every interface language so that presets work for everyone. See Computed column functions.

docs.title: How do I share presets with colleagues?
docs.text: Send the preset file with Export, or put presets in a shared folder that everyone adds under Settings › Read-only preset sources. See Export a preset and Use shared preset folders.

docs.title: Can I keep presets under version control?
docs.text: Yes. A preset is a plain-text .toml file, so it can be stored in Git or any versioned folder and compared line by line. See Preset file format.

docs.title: Can a preset run automatically every day?
docs.text: Yes. Configure execution on the Processing page creates a Windows scheduled task, or a .cmd launcher you double-click. Flash-Excel does not need to be open, but your Windows session does. See Schedule a preset.

docs.title: Why doesn't Flash-Excel run the schedule itself?
docs.text: Windows Task Scheduler does it better: a task survives a restart, runs without Flash-Excel being open and records each run's result. Configure execution creates that task for you. See Schedule a preset.

docs.title: Can I run a preset from a script?
docs.text: Yes, with Flash-Excel.exe --preset … --input …. See Command line.

docs.title: What happens to my presets when I update or uninstall?
docs.text: They stay. Presets, settings, outputs and logs are stored outside the installation folder, which is the only thing updates replace and uninstalling removes. See Data locations.

docs.title: Which version am I running?
docs.text: The version number is shown in the bottom-right corner of the window, for example v1.5.0. See Release notes for what changed.

docs.title: How do I switch the interface to French?
docs.text: Select Settings in the sidebar, then French under Language. See Change the language.

docs.title: Is Flash-Excel free?
docs.text: Yes. Flash-Excel is open source, under the MIT license. Its source code is on GitHub.

docs.title: Get started with Flash-Excel
docs.text: At the end of this page, you have installed Flash-Excel, built a preset with one step, checked it on a preview and written your first transformed file.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Windows PC. No administrator rights are needed: Flash-Excel installs for your Windows user only.
  • An Excel or CSV file to transform (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .csv).

docs.title: Install Flash-Excel
docs.text:
1. Open the latest release and download Flash-Excel-<version>-setup.exe.
  2. Run the installer and choose the wizard language. Flash-Excel starts in the language you pick here; you can change it later in Settings.
  3. Follow the wizard. Keep the launch option checked on the last page to start Flash-Excel right away.

The window opens on Processing. The sidebar on the left gives access to Processing, Presets and Settings.

docs.title: Build a preset with one step
docs.text:
A preset is the list of transformations to apply. This example renames one column.

  1. In the sidebar, select Presets.
  2. Next to Presets, select the + button (New preset). A new preset named Preset 1 (or the next free number) opens in the editor.
  3. In the name field at the top, type a name for the preset, for example My first preset.
  4. Under Load the Excel template, select Load a file and pick your source file. Flash-Excel reads its columns so the steps can offer them in their lists.
  5. Under Action configuration, select Rename columns in the list of actions.
  6. Select Add a rule. In Source column, pick the column to rename; in New name, type its new name.
  7. Select Save. The message Preset saved confirms it, and the preset appears in the list on the left.

docs.title: Preview and run the preset
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Processing.
  2. Click the drop zone Drop your Excel/CSV files here — or click to browse and pick your source file. You can also drag the file onto the window.
  3. Under Preset, open the list and select your preset.
  4. Select Preview. The Transformation preview window shows the first 100 rows of the file after the transformation, without writing anything. Close it with ×.
  5. Under Output, look at Destination folder: by default it is Documents\flash-excel\output. Leave it as is for this first run. If your source file is an .xls or .xlsm file, set Format to .xlsx (Excel): Same as source only writes .xlsx and .csv files.
  6. Select Run preset.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The file row shows the status Done, and the Console ends with a line such as Done in 0.42s → C:\Users\<you>\Documents\flash-excel\output\<file>_clean.xlsx. Open that folder: your transformed file is there, named after the source file with _clean added, and the source file is unchanged.

If the run ends with Error instead, the Console shows the reason. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 1.4.0 — 2026-10-18
docs.text:
Presets saved before 1.4.0 and CSV files

CSV separators are now detected automatically, but presets saved by earlier versions contain csv_separator = ";", which keeps forcing semicolons. If such a preset reads a comma-separated file as a single column, delete that line from the preset file. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Process several files in one run. Select or drop several files on the Processing page; each file has its own status in the queue, and On error › Stop all ends the whole run.
  • Drop files onto the window, on the Processing and Presets pages.
  • Preview shows the result of a preset on the first 100 rows without writing anything. See Preview a transformation.
  • Configure execution creates a daily Windows scheduled task or a .cmd launcher for a preset and its files. See Schedule a preset.
  • Command-line mode: Flash-Excel.exe --preset … --input … runs a preset without opening the window. See Command line.
  • Read-only preset sources in Settings: list presets from shared folders next to your own. See Use shared preset folders.
  • CSV output in Settings: choose the separator and decimal mark of output CSV files. Auto follows your Windows regional settings, so output files open in columns in Excel.
  • New preset option csv_decimal_comma to read 1,5 as a number in CSV source files.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• The separator of CSV source files is detected automatically instead of always being ;.
  • Column types of CSV files are guessed from every row, so a column that turns to text further down no longer makes the whole load fail.
  • Loading a large Excel template no longer freezes the window.
  • A damaged preset stays in the list, marked unreadable, instead of disappearing.
  • Save tells you when steps were refused and left out of the file.
  • Output files go to Documents\flash-excel\output by default, and the Destination folder field shows that full path.
  • Filter rows with contains matches the text exactly as typed: C++ no longer matches C+ dev.
  • A non-numeric value in a filter on a numeric column gives a clear message.
  • The palette cards in Settings preview the selected mode.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Presets using Value above or Value below in Fill empty cells could not be read back after saving and vanished from the list.
  • The template file name was lost each time a preset was saved.
  • Renaming a preset could lose it if the save failed, and two names differing only by punctuation overwrote each other.
  • Without a chosen destination, output files were written to the installation folder and lost at the next update.
  • A run on a file locked by Excel with On error › Ignore never ended.
  • DROITE(column, 0) returned the whole text instead of an empty text.
Maintenance version with no user-visible changes. It was not distributed through automatic updates.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Each entry starts from what you see. Error messages appear in the Console of the Processing page, in a message at the bottom of the window, or on the command line.

Where to find more detail

Every run, error and update check is recorded in the log file %LOCALAPPDATA%\flash-excel\logs\flash-excel.log. Paste that path into the address bar of File Explorer to open it. See Data locations.

docs.title: Unsupported format: 'xls'
docs.text:
Symptom — A run on an .xls or .xlsm file fails with Unsupported format: 'xls'. Expected 'xlsx', 'csv', or 'parquet'. (or 'xlsm'), after the steps have run.

Cause — Format is set to Same as source. Flash-Excel reads .xls and .xlsm files but cannot write them.

Fix

  1. On the Processing page, under Output, set Format to .xlsx (Excel).
  2. Select Run preset again.

On the command line, add --format xlsx. See File formats.

docs.title: Unsupported file format. Allowed: .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm, .csv
docs.text:
Symptom — Loading a file shows File error: followed by this message, or a dropped file is not added to the queue.

Cause — The file has another extension, for example .txt, .ods or .xlsb.

Fix — Open the file in Excel and save it as .xlsx or .csv, then load that copy.

docs.title: Excel file contains no readable sheets
docs.text:
Symptom — A run or a preview fails with Excel file contains no readable sheets.

Cause — The workbook has no sheet Flash-Excel can read, or the file is damaged.

Fix — Open the workbook in Excel, check that its first sheet holds the data, and save it again as .xlsx. Flash-Excel reads the first sheet only.

docs.title: A CSV source loads as a single column
docs.text:
Symptom — The template shows one column whose name contains the whole header line, such as name,age,city. Runs then fail with "…" not found or unable to find column.

Cause — The CSV is read with the wrong separator. Either the preset forces one with csv_separator — presets saved before version 1.4.0 contain csv_separator = ";" — or the separator could not be detected and ; was used.

Fix

  1. Open the preset file (Documents\flash-excel\presets\<name>.toml) in a text editor such as Notepad.
  2. In [meta], delete the csv_separator line to let Flash-Excel detect the separator, or set it to the file's separator, for example csv_separator = ",".
  3. Save the file and run again.

See Preset file format.

docs.title: Accented letters appear as � in a CSV source
docs.text:
Symptom — After loading or processing a CSV file, letters such as é or ç show as �.

Cause — The file is not encoded in UTF-8. Excel's CSV (separator: semicolon) and CSV (comma delimited) formats save in the Windows encoding (Windows-1252 on Western-European systems), while Flash-Excel reads UTF-8 by default.

Fix — In the preset file, add csv_encoding = "cp1252" to [meta], then run again. Alternatively, save the file from Excel as CSV UTF-8 (comma delimited). See Preset file format.

docs.title: Decimal numbers stay text in a CSV source
docs.text:
Symptom — A column of numbers such as 1,5 is treated as text: sorting is alphabetical, and Cast types to Decimal number fails with conversion from str to f64 failed.

Cause — The file uses a comma as decimal mark. Flash-Excel reads a dot as decimal mark unless told otherwise.

Fix — In the preset file, add csv_decimal_comma = true to [meta]. See Preset file format.

docs.title: An output CSV opens in a single column in Excel
docs.text:
Symptom — Double-clicking an output .csv file opens Excel with all values in column A.

Cause — The file's separator or decimal mark does not match the regional settings of the PC that opens it. This happens when CSV output is forced to a value, or when the file is opened on a PC with other regional settings than the one that wrote it.

Fix

  1. Select Settings in the sidebar.
  2. Under CSV output, set Column separator and Decimal mark to Auto to match this PC, or to the values the receiving PC expects.
  3. Run the preset again.

To open an existing file without re-running, use Excel's Data › From Text/CSV and choose the separator. See Set the CSV output format.

docs.title: Accented letters look wrong in an output CSV opened in Excel
docs.text:
Symptom — An output .csv opened by double-click in Excel shows Ã© instead of é.

Cause — Output CSV files are written in UTF-8. On a double-click, Excel may read them with the Windows encoding instead.

Fix — Choose .xlsx (Excel) as output Format when the file is meant for Excel. To open the CSV as it is, use Data › From Text/CSV in Excel and choose 65001: Unicode (UTF-8) as file origin.

docs.title: Permission denied, or the file is being used by another process
docs.text:
Symptom — A file fails with a message such as Permission denied or being used by another process. Its status becomes Error.

Cause — The output file (or, less often, the source file) is open in Excel or another program, which locks it.

Fix — Close the file in Excel, then run again. With Skip file, the other files of the run are processed anyway; only the locked one needs a new run.

docs.title: A step cannot find a column
docs.text:
Symptom — A step fails with "Amount" not found or unable to find column "Amount"; valid columns: [...].

Cause — The step names a column that does not exist at that point: the source file has different column names than the template, the name differs by case or spaces, or an earlier step renamed or removed the column.

Fix

  1. Compare the column names of the source file with those in the message's list of valid columns.
  2. On the Presets page, load the current file under Load the Excel template. If the Column layout changed dialog opens, select Load & clean up references to remove the missing columns from the steps, then fix the steps that need them.
  3. Select Save, then run again.

See Steps and their order.

docs.title: A computed column says a name is not available
docs.text:
Symptom — The Add computed column step fails with Expression not allowed: '…' is not available. Use column names or catalog functions.

Cause — The expression contains a name that is neither a column at this step nor a function. Common reasons: a typo, a function written in lower case (si instead of SI), or a column renamed or removed by an earlier step.

Fix — Write function names in upper case, wrap column names that contain spaces or symbols in brackets ([Unit price]), and use the column's name as it is at this step. Selecting the column under Columns in the editor inserts the right form. See Computed column functions.

docs.title: Invalid syntax in a computed column
docs.text:
Symptom — The Add computed column step fails with Invalid syntax: followed by details.

Cause — A parenthesis or a quote is not closed, a comma is missing between arguments, = is used instead of ==, or a bracketed name such as [Unit price] matches no column.

Fix — Check the punctuation of the expression and the exact spelling of bracketed column names. See Computed column functions.

docs.title: The truth value of an Expr is ambiguous
docs.text:
Symptom — The Add computed column step fails with Evaluation error: the truth value of an Expr is ambiguous.

Cause — The expression combines conditions with and, or, not or in.

Fix — Use & for and, | for or and ~ for not, with each comparison in parentheses: SI((age >= 18) & (age < 65), "working age", "other").

docs.title: '…' is not a number, but the column holds numbers
docs.text:
Symptom — Filter rows fails with '18 years' is not a number, but the column holds numbers (Int64). Enter a numeric value.

Cause — A condition on a numeric column has a value that is not a number.

Fix — On the Presets page, open Filter rows and type only the number in Value, with a dot as decimal mark (18, 1.5). Then select Save.

docs.title: Conversion from str to … failed
docs.text:
Symptom — Cast types fails with conversion from str to i64 failed in column 'amount' for 3 out of 1250 values: [...]. The type may also read f64, date or datetime[μs].

Cause — Some values cannot be converted: text in a number column, a comma as decimal mark, a decimal number cast to Whole number, or a date that is not in YYYY-MM-DD form. The message lists the values that failed.

Fix — Clean those values in the steps before Cast types, for example with Replace values or Clean text, or cast to another type. See Steps › Cast types.

docs.title: Expected String in Clean text or a text function
docs.text:
Symptom — Clean text, or a text function such as MAJUSCULE, fails with invalid series dtype: expected String, got i64.

Cause — The column holds numbers or dates, not text.

Fix — Add the column to Cast types with type Text. Cast types runs before Clean text and computed columns.

docs.title: The output has fewer rows than expected
docs.text:
Symptom — The output, or the preview, has fewer rows than expected, or none at all.

Cause — Filter rows removes rows whose cells are empty in a filtered column, and text comparisons are case-sensitive (Active does not match active). Deduplicate rows also removes rows. The preview works on the first 100 rows only, so it may show No rows remain in this sample after transformation while the full file still has matching rows.

Fix — Check the filter values' case and spelling; clean the text first with Clean text if needed. Run the preset on the whole file to see the real result.

docs.title: A preset is marked unreadable
docs.text:
Symptom — A preset appears in the list with the marker unreadable, and cannot be opened or run.

Cause — Its file is not a valid preset: invalid TOML syntax, or a missing or wrong value. This usually follows a hand edit. Hover over the marker to read the exact reason, such as contains invalid TOML syntax or contains configuration errors.

Fix

  1. Open the file in Documents\flash-excel\presets with a text editor.
  2. Fix the line named in the reason. Steps are numbered from 0 in the message.
  3. Save the file. The preset becomes readable the next time the list is loaded.

See Preset file format.

docs.title: Preset saved, but these steps were refused
docs.text:
Symptom — Save shows Preset saved, but these steps were refused and are not in the file: followed by step names.

Cause — Those steps were incomplete or had values a preset does not accept, for example a step with no column selected. The preset was saved without them.

Fix — Open each named step, complete it or clear it, then select Save again.

docs.title: A preset already uses the file
docs.text:
Symptom — Save fails with A preset already uses the file '…'. Choose another name.

Cause — Two preset names that differ only by punctuation or case give the same file name (Sales report! and sales report both give sales_report.toml).

Fix — Give the preset a name that differs by at least one letter or digit.

docs.title: The preset holds a value that cannot be saved to TOML
docs.text:
Symptom — Save fails with The preset '…' holds a value that cannot be saved to TOML (a null inside a step).

Cause — A step contains an empty value that a preset file cannot store, typically a Replace values rule whose Replace with is empty.

Fix — Give the rule a replacement value, or remove it, then select Save again.

docs.title: Changes to a preset are not used by the run
docs.text:
Symptom — Preview or Run preset behaves as if your latest changes to the steps were not there.

Cause — Runs and previews use the preset as saved on disk.

Fix — On the Presets page, select Save, then go back to Processing and select the preset again.

docs.title: Shared presets are missing, or cannot be saved or exported
docs.text:
Symptom — Presets from a shared folder do not appear in the list; or, for a shared preset, Save and Delete are disabled and Export fails with Preset file is outside the presets directory.

Cause — A shared folder that cannot be reached (network drive disconnected, folder moved) is skipped; the log records preset source unavailable. Shared presets are read-only by design and cannot be exported from Flash-Excel.

Fix — Check that the folder opens in File Explorer, and correct its Folder path under Settings › Read-only preset sources if needed. To get your own editable copy of a shared preset, copy its .toml file into Documents\flash-excel\presets with File Explorer. See Use shared preset folders.

docs.title: A run is already in progress
docs.text:
Symptom — Starting a run shows A run is already in progress.

Cause — A previous run has not finished yet.

Fix — Wait for it to end, or stop it with the square button next to Run preset. See Stop a run.

docs.title: The scheduled task did not run
docs.text:
Symptom — No output file was written at the scheduled time.

Cause — Possible causes:

  • Tasks created by Flash-Excel run only while your Windows session is open. They do not run when you are signed out or the PC is off, and a missed time is not caught up later.
  • A preset or input file was moved, renamed or deleted after the task was created: the task uses the exact paths it was created with.
  • A file failed: the run went on with the other files, and the task ended with result 0x1.

Fix

  1. Open Task Scheduler, then Task Scheduler Library › Flash-Excel, and select the task. Check Last Run Time and Last Run Result.
  2. Open the log file and look for lines ending in FAILED at that time.
  3. If paths changed, create the task again from Configure execution on the Processing page.

See Schedule a preset.

docs.title: The scheduling command is too long
docs.text:
Symptom — Advanced: copy the scheduling command warns that Windows cannot create this task with a pasted /tr command because it exceeds 261 characters.

Cause — With many or long file paths, the command exceeds the length Windows accepts for a pasted schtasks command.

Fix — Select Add to Task Scheduler instead: Flash-Excel then registers the full configuration itself, without that limit.

docs.title: Scheduling commands cannot contain %, !, quotes or newlines
docs.text:
Symptom — Add to Task Scheduler or Create a .cmd launcher fails with this message.

Cause — A path, the output folder or the naming pattern contains %, ! or ". These characters change meaning in Windows commands.

Fix — Rename the files or folders concerned, or choose another output folder or naming pattern, then try again.

docs.title: Enter a name of 1–200 characters without reserved filename characters
docs.text:
Symptom — Creating a scheduled task or a launcher fails with this message.

Cause — Execution name is empty, too long, ends with a dot or a space, or contains one of \ / : * ? " < > | % !.

Fix — Enter a plain name, for example Monthly HR report.

docs.title: Start time must use HH:mm
docs.text:
Symptom — Add to Task Scheduler fails with Start time must use HH:mm (00:00–23:59).

Fix — Enter the Daily time (scheduled task) as two-digit hours and minutes, for example 07:30.

docs.title: No output in the Command Prompt
docs.text:
Symptom — A command-line run prints nothing, or the prompt comes back before the run ends.

Cause — Flash-Excel is a windowed program: it writes to a console only when started from one, and an interactive prompt may not wait for it.

Fix — Run the command from a .cmd batch file, which waits for it and can read %ERRORLEVEL%, and check the log file for the result of each file. See Command line.

docs.title: The update link never appears, or the update fails
docs.text:
Symptom — No Update to v… link appears although a newer version exists, or selecting it shows Updating… and then nothing changes.

Cause — The update server could not be reached (no internet connection, proxy or firewall), or the downloaded update did not pass the signature check. The log records update check FAILED or update apply FAILED with the reason.

Fix

  1. Check your internet connection and restart Flash-Excel: the check runs at each start.
  2. If it still fails, download the latest Flash-Excel-<version>-setup.exe from the GitHub releases page and run it. Your presets and settings are kept.

See Automatic updates and Update Flash-Excel.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Open an issue on GitHub with the error message, what you were doing, and the matching lines of the log file. Remove any confidential data from them first.

docs.text:
These pages explain the few notions you need to use Flash-Excel with confidence. They contain no steps: each one links to the guides that put it into practice.

docs.title: Automatic updates
docs.text: Flash-Excel keeps itself up to date from inside the application. You do not need to download a new installer for each version.

docs.title: How a new version is found
docs.text:
Each time Flash-Excel starts, it asks the update server whether a newer version exists. The check runs in the background and does not slow down your work.

When a newer version is available, the bottom-right corner of the window shows Update to vX.Y.Z next to the current version number. Nothing is installed until you select it. When no update is available, or when the check cannot reach the server (for example without an internet connection), only the version number is shown.

docs.title: How an update is installed
docs.text:
When you select Update to vX.Y.Z, the link changes to Updating… while Flash-Excel:

  1. downloads the new version — often as a small patch rather than the whole application;
  2. checks that the download is genuine;
  3. closes the window, so that its files can be replaced, and installs the new version in its installation folder.

Start Flash-Excel again if it does not reopen by itself. No administrator rights are needed, because Flash-Excel is installed for your Windows user only.

docs.title: Signed updates
docs.text: Every release is signed by the publisher, and the update metadata is signed too (Flash-Excel uses The Update Framework, a standard for secure software updates). Before installing anything, Flash-Excel checks those signatures against the trusted keys shipped with the application. A download that was altered, or that does not come from the publisher, is refused and nothing is installed.

docs.title: What an update keeps
docs.text: An update replaces only the installation folder. Your settings, presets, output files and logs are stored elsewhere and are left untouched. See Data locations.

docs.title: When automatic updates do not apply
docs.text: Updates only work in the installed application. If an update fails, the reason is written to the application log, and you can always install the latest version by hand from the GitHub releases page. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: A run can fail for a file — the file is open in Excel, a step refers to a column that is missing, a value cannot be converted. The On error choice on the Processing page decides what Flash-Excel does next. It matters most when you process several files in one run.

docs.title: The three choices
docs.text:
Choice (as shown in the app) When a step fails Rest of the run Skip file — continue queue (default) Processing of this file stops. No output file is written for it. Its status becomes Skipped. The next files are processed. Stop all — halt on first error Processing of this file stops. No output file is written for it. Its status becomes Error. The whole run ends. Files not yet processed are marked Skipped. Ignore — write partial The failing step is left out: the data passes through it unchanged. The following steps still run and the output file is written. The next files are processed.

With Ignore, the output is partial: it lacks the effect of every step that failed. Check the Console before you use such a file.

docs.title: Errors outside the steps
docs.text:
Some errors happen before the first step or after the last one: the source file cannot be read (missing, locked by Excel, unreadable format), or the output file cannot be written. No output can be produced in that case, whatever the choice:

  • the file's status becomes Error;
  • with Skip file and Ignore, the next files are still processed;
  • with Stop all, the whole run ends.

docs.title: Where errors appear
docs.text:
• The Console at the bottom of the Processing page shows each error message, and Errors counts them. Warnings counts messages such as Skipping file due to error in '…'.
  • Each file in the queue shows its own status: Pending, Running, Done, Error or Skipped.
  • The application log keeps a trace of each run. See Data locations.

docs.title: Stopping a run yourself
docs.text: The stop button (the square next to Run preset) asks the run to stop. Flash-Excel finishes the step in progress, then stops: the current file is not written, and the files after it are not processed. The Console shows Run stopped by user. See Stop a run.

docs.title: Runs outside the window
docs.text: Launchers, scheduled tasks and the command line have no On error choice. They always behave like Skip file: a file that fails at any point gets no output, and the next files are still processed. The run then ends with exit code 1 instead of 0. See Command line.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text: A preset is a saved list of transformations. You build it once on the Presets page, then apply it to as many files as you like from the Processing page, from a launcher, from a scheduled task or from the command line. The source file is never modified: every run writes a new output file.

docs.title: What a preset contains
docs.text:
A preset is a small text file in the TOML format, with the .toml extension. It holds two parts:

  • Metadata — the preset name, an optional description, and options for reading CSV files (separator, encoding, decimal mark).
  • Steps — the ordered list of transformations: rename columns, filter rows, add a computed column, and so on. Flash-Excel offers 12 kinds of step. See Steps and their order.

The preset also remembers the columns and their types of the file you loaded under Load the Excel template. This is why you can reopen a preset and edit its steps without loading the file again: the editor shows Template model · file may no longer exist on this machine and keeps offering the remembered columns.

The full file format is described in Preset file format.

docs.title: Where presets are stored
docs.text:
The presets you create are saved in your Documents folder, under Documents\flash-excel\presets. The file name comes from the preset name: lower case, punctuation removed, spaces replaced by underscores. Monthly HR report is saved as monthly_hr_report.toml.

Because they live in Documents, presets survive updates and uninstallation, and you can back them up, copy them or send them like any other document. See Data locations.

docs.title: Local and shared presets
docs.text:
Flash-Excel lists presets from two kinds of places:

Kind Where it comes from What you can do Local Documents\flash-excel\presets Edit, save, delete, export, run. Shared A folder you add under Settings › Read-only preset sources, with a label Run and preview. Save and Delete are disabled.

Shared folders let a team use the same presets, for example from a network drive. Flash-Excel never writes to them: Shared folders are read-only in Flash-Excel. To change a shared preset, edit the file in the shared folder itself, or ask whoever maintains it. If a shared folder cannot be reached, its presets are simply not listed. See Use shared preset folders.

docs.title: Saved presets are what runs
docs.text:
Run preset and Preview read the preset file as it is saved on disk. Changes made in the editor apply only after you select Save on the Presets page.

A preset file that Flash-Excel cannot read still appears in the list, marked unreadable, so that a damaged file does not look like a deleted one. Hover over the marker to see the reason. See Troubleshooting.

Editing a preset file by hand

You can write or edit a preset file in a text editor. Keep in mind that saving that preset again from the Presets page rewrites its metadata: the description and the CSV reading options (csv_separator, csv_encoding, csv_decimal_comma) go back to their defaults. The editor also keeps only one step of each kind, in its own fixed order. See Steps and their order.

docs.title: Steps and their order
docs.text: A preset is a chain of steps. Each step does one kind of transformation — rename columns, filter rows, sort rows — and hands its result to the next one. The output file is what comes out of the last step.

docs.title: Steps run one after the other
docs.text:
Steps never see the source file directly: each one works on the result of the steps before it. This has three practical effects:

  • Removed columns are gone for later steps. After Select columns or Drop columns, a later step cannot use a column that was left out.
  • Renamed columns change name for later steps. After Rename columns, later steps refer to the new name.
  • Added columns exist only for later steps. A column created by Add computed column can be filtered, sorted or reordered, because those steps come after it.

The editor follows this chain for you. The column lists offered by each step show the columns as they are at that point, not as they are in the source file. When you rename a column, the steps after it are updated to use the new name. When a newly loaded template file no longer contains some columns, the Column layout changed dialog offers Load & clean up references to remove them from your steps.

If a step still refers to a column that no longer exists when the preset runs, that step fails and the file is handled according to the On error choice. See Error handling.

docs.title: The order used by the editor
docs.text:
On the Presets page, the Action configuration list shows the 12 kinds of step in a fixed order. You configure each kind at most once, and the preset runs the configured ones in this order:

Order Step (as shown in the app) Typical use 1 Rename columns Give the source columns the names you want to work with. 2 Select columns Keep only the columns you need. 3 Drop columns Remove a few columns. 4 Cast types Turn text into numbers, dates or booleans. 5 Replace values Swap exact values, such as codes for labels. 6 Clean text Trim spaces, remove accents, change case. 7 Fill empty cells Replace empty cells with a value or a neighbour. 8 Add computed column Build a new column from a formula. 9 Filter rows Keep only the rows that match conditions. 10 Deduplicate rows Remove duplicate rows. 11 Sort rows Order the rows. 12 Reorder columns Set the final column order.

A step you leave empty is not saved and does not run; if it was only partly filled in, Save tells you it was refused (Preset saved, but these steps were refused and are not in the file). The steps cannot be dragged into another order in the editor: the order above is designed so that each step finds the columns and types it needs.

Three kinds of step hold several rules: Replace values (one rule per column), Clean text (one clean action per group of columns) and Add computed column (one rule per new column). Each rule is saved as its own step, and the rules run from top to bottom.

For what each step does and accepts, see Steps reference.

docs.title: Presets written by hand
docs.text:
In a preset file you write yourself, steps run in the order they appear in the file, and the same kind of step may appear several times. That gives you full control, for example to filter rows before cleaning text.

Opening a hand-written preset in the editor

The editor shows one step of each kind. When a file repeats a kind that holds a single rule set (for example two Filter rows steps), the editor shows only the last one, and selecting Save writes the steps back in the editor's order above. Keep hand-written presets that rely on their own order out of the editor, or check them after saving.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Flash-Excel can apply a preset without opening its window. This is what launchers and scheduled tasks use, and you can call it yourself from a Command Prompt, a batch file or another tool. For a step-by-step guide, see Run from the command line.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
Flash-Excel.exe --preset <preset.toml> --input <file> [<file> …] [--output <folder>] [--format keep|xlsx|csv|parquet] [--pattern <pattern>] [--debug]

Flash-Excel.exe is the program in the Flash-Excel installation folder. The exact path on your PC is shown in the Schedule or create a launcher window, after Uses the installed application:. Use the full path, in quotes, when you call it from another folder.

There is only one program: given --preset, it runs without a window; without --preset, it opens the window as usual.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Required Default Description --preset <path> Yes — The .toml preset file to apply. Any preset file works: local, shared or elsewhere. --input <path> … Yes — One or more source files, separated by spaces. Each file is processed on its own. --output <folder> No Documents\flash-excel\output Destination folder, created if needed. A relative folder is placed inside Documents\flash-excel\output. --format <format> No keep Output format: keep (same as the source file), xlsx, csv or parquet. --pattern <text> No {name}_clean Name of each output file, without extension. {name} is replaced by the source file name without its extension. --debug No off Writes detailed messages to the log file. -h, --help No — Shows the list of options. Must be combined with --preset to reach the command-line mode, for example Flash-Excel.exe --preset x --help.

Paths containing spaces must be in double quotes.

docs.title: Output file names
docs.text:
With the defaults, C:\Data\sales.xlsx gives Documents\flash-excel\output\sales_clean.xlsx. An existing file with the same name is replaced.

keep reuses the source file's extension. It works for .xlsx and .csv sources. For .xls and .xlsm sources, Flash-Excel cannot write that format and the file fails with Unsupported format: 'xls': pass --format xlsx. See File formats.

docs.title: Settings used from the app
docs.text:
A command-line run uses the settings saved in the app:

  • the CSV output settings (Column separator and Decimal mark) for CSV output files;
  • the Language, for the true/false labels in Excel output files (True/False in English, VRAI/FAUX in French).

The preset's own [meta] options decide how CSV source files are read. See Settings and Preset file format.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Files are processed one after the other, in the order given.
  • A file that fails — unreadable, locked by Excel, a step error, an output that cannot be written — gets no output file. The next files are still processed. There is no equivalent of the window's On error choice.
  • If the preset itself cannot be loaded, nothing is processed.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
For each file, one line is printed and written to the log file:

sales.xlsx -> C:\Users\me\Documents\flash-excel\output\sales_clean.xlsx (1250 rows)
march.csv FAILED: No such file or directory (os error 2): ...

Successful files are reported on the standard output, failed ones on the standard error.

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Flash-Excel is a windowed program. When you start it from a Command Prompt or PowerShell, it writes its messages into that console. When nothing started it from a console — a scheduled task, a double-click — there is no console and the messages go only to the log file. The exit code is set in every case.

Waiting for the end of the run

A batch file (.cmd or .bat) waits for each program it starts, so it can read the exit code in %ERRORLEVEL%. This is how the launchers created by Flash-Excel work. In an interactive prompt, Windows may give the prompt back before a windowed program ends: run the command from a batch file when you need the exit code.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Every input file was processed and written. 1 At least one input file failed, or the preset could not be loaded (file not found, invalid preset). 2 Invalid command line: a required option is missing, an option is unknown, or --format has another value.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Apply a preset to one file, with the default output folder and format:

Flash-Excel.exe --preset "%USERPROFILE%\Documents\flash-excel\presets\monthly_hr_report.toml" --input "C:\Exports\hr.xlsx"

Process three files into a CSV in a chosen folder:

Flash-Excel.exe --preset clean.toml --input jan.xlsx feb.xlsx mar.xlsx --output "D:\Reports\Q1" --format csv

Name the outputs after the month and convert .xls sources to .xlsx:

Flash-Excel.exe --preset clean.toml --input "C:\Exports\report.xls" --format xlsx --pattern "{name}_2026-10"

Use the exit code in a batch file:

@echo off
"C:\path\to\Flash-Excel.exe" --preset clean.toml --input a.xlsx b.xlsx
if errorlevel 1 echo At least one file failed. See the log file.
