docs.title: Computed column functions
docs.text:
The Add computed column step builds a new column from a formula, called an expression. The expression is computed for every row. This page lists everything an expression can contain.

Function names are in French, after the French version of Excel (CONCATENER for CONCAT, SI for IF). Type them exactly as shown, in upper case.

docs.title: Writing an expression
docs.text:
An expression combines column references, literal values, operators and functions:

SI([Unit price] * qty > 1000, "large", "small")

The editor helps you build it: selecting a chip under Columns, Functions or Separators appends it to the end of the expression. You still type the commas between arguments and the closing parentheses yourself. Hovering over a function shows its description and an Example.

docs.title: Column references
docs.text:
Syntax When to use it Example name The column name contains only letters, digits and underscores, and does not start with a digit. last_name [Column Name] Any other name: spaces, a leading digit, symbols such as °, € or -. [Unit price] col("Column Name") Same as brackets. Also works when a column has the same name as a function. col("ABS")

The Columns chips add brackets for you when a name needs them. A name in brackets must match an existing column exactly; otherwise the expression is refused with Invalid syntax.

A column reference uses the columns as they are at this step: renamed columns go by their new name, and an earlier computed column can be used by a later one.

docs.title: Literal values
docs.text:
Kind How to write it Example Text Between double or single quotes "adult", ' - ' Number Digits, with a dot as decimal mark 18, 1.2 Boolean True or False True

An expression must use at least one column or function. A literal on its own, such as "N/A" or 0, is refused with The expression must return a Polars Expr. To fill a column with a fixed text, write CONCATENER("N/A").

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Example + - * / Add, subtract, multiply, divide [Unit price] * qty // % ** Whole division, remainder, power qty % 2 - (in front) Negative value -delta + between texts Joins two texts MAJUSCULE(code) + "-FR" == != < > <= >= Comparisons; produce true or false age >= 18 & | ~ And, or, not — to combine comparisons (age >= 18) & (age < 65) ( ) Grouping (a + b) * 2
  • Equality is ==. A single = is refused with Invalid syntax.
  • Combine conditions with & and |, and put each comparison in parentheses. The words and, or, not and in do not work on columns and fail with the truth value of an Expr is ambiguous.
  • Dividing by zero gives an infinite value, not an error.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Function Category Signature Returns CONCATENER Text CONCATENER(part1, part2, …, sep="") The parts joined into one text. MAJUSCULE Text MAJUSCULE(text) The text in upper case. MINUSCULE Text MINUSCULE(text) The text in lower case. GAUCHE Text GAUCHE(text, n) The first n characters. DROITE Text DROITE(text, n) The last n characters. NBCAR Text NBCAR(text) The number of characters. SUPPRESPACE Text SUPPRESPACE(text) The text without leading and trailing whitespace. ARRONDI Math ARRONDI(number, n=0) The number rounded to n decimal places. ABS Math ABS(number) The absolute value. MULTIPLIER Math MULTIPLIER(number, n) The number multiplied by n. AJOUTER Math AJOUTER(number1, number2) The sum of the two values. ANNEE Date ANNEE(date) The year. MOIS Date MOIS(date) The month, from 1 to 12. JOUR Date JOUR(date) The day of the month. AUJOURD_HUI Date AUJOURD_HUI() Today's date, on the day the preset runs. SI Logic SI(condition, then, else) then where the condition is true, else elsewhere.

Arguments shown as text, number or date accept a column reference or another function call. n is a number you type.

docs.title: CONCATENER
docs.text:
Joins columns and texts into one text. Number columns are converted to text. The optional sep is inserted between every two parts.

CONCATENER(first_name, " ", last_name)      → "Ann Smith"
CONCATENER(year, month, day, sep="-")       → "2024-3-5"

If any part is empty for a row, the result is empty for that row. Fill empty cells first with Fill empty cells.

docs.title: MAJUSCULE
docs.text:
Converts every character to upper case.

MAJUSCULE(last_name)                        → "SMITH"

docs.title: MINUSCULE
docs.text:
Converts every character to lower case.

MINUSCULE(email)                            → "ann.smith@example.com"

docs.title: GAUCHE
docs.text:
Returns the first n characters. GAUCHE(code, 0) returns an empty text.

GAUCHE(code, 3)                             → "FR-" for "FR-1234"

docs.title: DROITE
docs.text:
Returns the last n characters. DROITE(reference, 0) returns an empty text.

DROITE(reference, 4)                        → "1234" for "FR-1234"

docs.title: NBCAR
docs.text:
Returns the number of characters, spaces included.

NBCAR(description)                          → 11 for "Hello world"

docs.title: SUPPRESPACE
docs.text:
Removes whitespace at the start and end of the text. Spaces inside the text are kept; to collapse them, use the Clean text step.

SUPPRESPACE(last_name)                      → "Smith" for "  Smith "

docs.title: ARRONDI
docs.text:
Rounds to n decimal places. Without n, rounds to a whole number.

ARRONDI(price, 2)                           → 1.23 for 1.234
ARRONDI(price)                              → 1.0 for 1.234

docs.title: ABS
docs.text:
Returns the absolute value, always positive or zero.

ABS(delta)                                  → 5 for -5

docs.title: MULTIPLIER
docs.text:
Multiplies every value by n. Same as price * 1.2.

MULTIPLIER(price, 1.2)                      → 120 for 100

docs.title: AJOUTER
docs.text:
Adds two values: two numeric columns, or a column and a number. Same as base + bonus.

AJOUTER(base, bonus)                        → 1200 for 1000 and 200

docs.title: ANNEE
docs.text:
Extracts the year. The column must hold dates or dates and times; cast a text column first with Cast types.

ANNEE(birth_date)                           → 1990

docs.title: MOIS
docs.text:
Extracts the month, from 1 to 12.

MOIS(order_date)                            → 3 for 2024-03-05

docs.title: JOUR
docs.text:
Extracts the day of the month.

JOUR(delivery_date)                         → 5 for 2024-03-05

docs.title: AUJOURD_HUI
docs.text:
Returns the date of the day the preset runs. It takes no argument but still needs its parentheses. The editor's chip shows it as AUJOURD'HUI; in the expression, write AUJOURD_HUI() with an underscore.

AUJOURD_HUI()                               → 2026-10-21

docs.title: SI
docs.text:
Returns then where the condition is true and else everywhere else. then and else can be columns, texts or numbers. The condition uses the comparison operators ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, combined if needed with &, | and ~.

SI(age >= 18, "adult", "minor")
SI((qty > 1) & (qty < 10), "batch", "single")
SI(status == "Active", salary, 0)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
When an expression cannot be computed, the step fails. The Console shows one of these messages:

Message Cause Fix Invalid syntax: Unbalanced parentheses or quotes, a missing comma, = instead of ==, or [Name] that matches no column. Check the punctuation; check the bracketed column name. Expression not allowed: '…' is not available. Use column names or catalog functions. A name that is neither a column at this step nor a function: a typo, a wrong case, or a column renamed or removed earlier. Fix the name, or use [Column Name]. Function names are upper case. Expression not allowed: (other text) The expression uses a construct that is not allowed. Use only the functions and operators on this page. Evaluation error: A function is missing an argument (missing 1 required positional argument), or and/or/in was used instead of &/|. Check the function's signature on this page. invalid series dtype: expected String, … operation not supported for dtype … A function received a column of the wrong type: MAJUSCULE on a number, ANNEE on text, ABS on text. Convert the column first with Cast types. The expression must return a Polars Expr The expression is a plain value, with no column or function. Wrap the value, for example CONCATENER("N/A").

See also Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Data locations
docs.text: Flash-Excel keeps your data outside its installation folder, so that updates — which replace that folder — never touch it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What Location Contents Presets Documents\flash-excel\presets Your local presets, one .toml file each. Output files (default) Documents\flash-excel\output Files written by runs when no other folder is chosen. Settings %APPDATA%\flash-excel app.config.yaml, theme.config.yaml and window data. Logs %LOCALAPPDATA%\flash-excel\logs flash-excel.log and its archives. Shared presets The folders listed under Read-only preset sources Presets maintained by someone else. Flash-Excel only reads them. Program The installation folder The application itself. Replaced by every update.

To open one of these folders, paste its location — for example %APPDATA%\flash-excel — into the address bar of File Explorer.

docs.title: Presets and output files
docs.text:
Documents is your real Documents folder, including when it is redirected to OneDrive (%USERPROFILE%\OneDrive\Documents). Presets and outputs are ordinary documents: open them, back them up, copy them to another PC.

The output folder is only the default. Each run can write elsewhere: Destination folder on the Processing page, or --output on the command line. A relative folder is created inside Documents\flash-excel\output.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
%APPDATA% is your roaming application data folder, usually C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming. It contains:

File or folder Contents app.config.yaml Palette, mode, language, CSV output and shared preset folders. See Settings. theme.config.yaml The colour palettes. theme.config.yaml.bak is the previous copy, kept when an update changes them. .theme.source Marker used to detect a newer palette file. Do not edit. webview\ Data of the application window. installer.ini Written by the installer with the language chosen in the wizard, read once at the next start, then deleted.

If you delete app.config.yaml, Flash-Excel creates it again with the default settings at the next start.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
%LOCALAPPDATA% is your local application data folder, usually C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local. The log file %LOCALAPPDATA%\flash-excel\logs\flash-excel.log records starts, runs, errors and update checks.

  • A new log file is started every day; the previous one is renamed with its date and time.
  • Log files older than 14 days are deleted.
  • To record more detail, start Flash-Excel with --debug, or add --debug to a command-line run.

The log is the first place to look when something fails. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Program
docs.text: Flash-Excel installs for your Windows user only, by default under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs, without administrator rights. Do not store anything in the installation folder: every update replaces it.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
Uninstall Flash-Excel from Settings › Apps in Windows (or Programs and Features). Uninstalling removes the installation folder only.

Kept after uninstalling Removed Presets (Documents\flash-excel\presets) The program files Output files (Documents\flash-excel\output and any other folder you used) Settings (%APPDATA%\flash-excel) Logs (%LOCALAPPDATA%\flash-excel\logs) Scheduled tasks and .cmd launchers you created

Reinstalling later picks up your presets and settings again. To remove everything, delete these folders by hand after uninstalling, and remove your scheduled tasks from the Flash-Excel folder of Task Scheduler (see Schedule a preset).

docs.title: Presets from versions before 1.3.0
docs.text: Versions before 1.3.0 stored presets inside the installation folder. On its first start, a newer version copies any preset still found there to Documents\flash-excel\presets, without overwriting a preset of the same name. Settings from those versions are not carried over.

docs.title: Source files (read)
docs.text:
Format Extensions What is read Excel workbook .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls The first sheet only. Its first row gives the column names. CSV (delimited text) .csv The whole file. Its first line gives the column names.

The file pickers and the drop zone accept only these four extensions. Another file is refused with Unsupported file format. Allowed: .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm, .csv.

docs.title: Excel files
docs.text:
• Only the first sheet of the workbook is read; the other sheets are ignored. To process another sheet, move it to the first position in Excel and save.
  • Cells containing formulas are read as their last calculated values.
  • Formatting (colours, fonts, column widths, merged cells) is not read.
  • The workbook must not be locked by another program while it is read. If Excel holds it open, the file fails; close it in Excel and run again.

docs.title: CSV files
docs.text:
Aspect Behaviour Preset option Separator Detected from the start of the file among ;, ,, tab and |. When detection is not conclusive, ; is used. csv_separator forces one. Encoding UTF-8. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (for example accented letters saved in Windows-1252) become �. csv_encoding, e.g. "cp1252". Decimal mark Dot: 1.5 is a number, 1,5 stays text. csv_decimal_comma = true. Column types Guessed from every row of the file: a column is numeric only if all its values are numbers. Dates stay text until you cast them. — Empty fields Read as empty cells, which Fill empty cells can fill. —

The preset options are described in Preset file format. From the command line, a source file whose extension is not an Excel one is read as CSV.

Column types in the editor

To keep the editor fast, the column types it shows for a CSV template are guessed from the first 300 rows. A run reads every row, so a column that changes from numbers to text further down is text in the run even if the editor showed it as a number.

docs.title: Output files (write)
docs.text:
On the Processing page, Format offers four choices; on the command line, --format takes the matching value.

Format (in the app) --format Extension written Notes Same as source keep Same as the source file Works for .xlsx and .csv sources only. See the warning below. .xlsx (Excel) xlsx .xlsx One sheet. Dates as DD/MM/YYYY, dates and times as DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS. True/false values written as text in the interface language: True/False or VRAI/FAUX. .csv (UTF-8) csv .csv UTF-8 text with a header line. Separator and decimal mark from Settings › CSV output. .parquet parquet .parquet Columnar data file for data tools (Power BI, Python, databases). Keeps column types exactly.

Same as source with .xls and .xlsm files

Flash-Excel cannot write the old .xls format, nor macro-enabled .xlsm workbooks. With Same as source, such a source file fails with Unsupported format: 'xls' (or 'xlsm') after all steps have run. Choose .xlsx (Excel) for these files.

docs.title: Name and location
docs.text:
• The output is written to the Destination folder (default Documents\flash-excel\output). A relative folder is placed inside that default folder.
  • Its name follows the Naming pattern (default {name}_clean), where {name} is the source file name without its extension: sales.xlsx gives sales_clean.xlsx.
  • An existing file with the same name is replaced without warning. Choose a pattern that differs from {name} if the output goes to the source folder, so the source file is not overwritten.
  • The source file itself is never modified otherwise.

Formatting, formulas, other sheets and macros of the source are not carried over to the output: the output holds values only.

See also Data locations and Set the CSV output format.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Action name The technical name of a kind of step in a preset file, such as filter_rows for Filter rows. See Steps. Batch Several source files processed in one run with the same preset. Each file is processed and written on its own. Computed column A column created by the Add computed column step from an expression. See Computed column functions. Console The panel at the bottom of the Processing page that shows the messages of a run: files loaded, steps applied, warnings and errors. Destination folder The folder where a run writes its output files. Default: Documents\flash-excel\output. Error mode What a run does when a file or a step fails, set under On error: Skip file, Stop all or Ignore. See Error handling. Expression The formula of a computed column, for example CONCATENER(first_name, " ", last_name). Headless run A run without the window, started from the command line, a launcher or a scheduled task. See Command line. Launcher A .cmd file created by Flash-Excel that runs a preset on fixed files when you double-click it. See Create a launcher. Local preset A preset stored in Documents\flash-excel\presets, which you can edit, save, delete and export. Naming pattern The name given to output files, without extension. {name} stands for the source file name. Default: {name}_clean. Output file The file a run writes. The source file is not changed. Palette A set of interface colours (Blue Gray, GitHub, Warm Dark), each with a dark and a light mode. Preset A saved list of steps, stored as a .toml file, that you apply to source files. See Presets. Preview The result of a preset on the first 100 rows of a file, shown without writing anything. See Preview a transformation. Queue The list of source files loaded on the Processing page, each with its status: Pending, Running, Done, Error or Skipped. Read-only preset source A shared folder added in Settings whose presets are listed next to yours but cannot be changed from Flash-Excel. See Use shared preset folders. Scheduled task A Windows Task Scheduler task that runs a preset every day at a set time. See Schedule a preset. Source file An Excel or CSV file you apply a preset to. Step One transformation in a preset, such as Rename columns or Sort rows. Flash-Excel offers 12 kinds of step. See Steps and their order. Template file The file loaded under Load the Excel template on the Presets page. It supplies the column names and types the step editors offer. The preset remembers them, so the file is not needed afterwards. TOML The plain-text format of preset files. See Preset file format.

docs.title: Preset file format
docs.text: A preset is a text file in the TOML format, saved with the .toml extension and encoded in UTF-8. The Presets page writes these files for you; this page describes their format, for reading them, sharing them or writing one by hand. For what a preset is, see Presets.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A preset file has one [meta] table followed by any number of [[steps]] tables:

[meta]
name = "My preset"

[[steps]]
action = "drop_columns"
columns = ["tmp"]

[[steps]]
action = "sort_rows"
by = ["date"]

Steps run in the order they appear in the file. A preset with no steps is valid: it copies the data unchanged into the output format.

docs.title: The [meta] table
docs.text:
Key Type Required Default Description name text Yes — Name shown in the preset lists. description text No "" Free description, for your own notes. The app does not display it. csv_separator text No (not set) Column separator used to read CSV source files, for example ";", ",", "\t" or "|". When not set, Flash-Excel detects it from the file. csv_encoding text No "utf8-lossy" Encoding used to read CSV source files. See below. csv_decimal_comma true / false No false Read 1,5 as the number 1.5 in CSV source files. Turn it on only for files that use a comma as decimal mark. source_columns list of text No [] Columns of the template file. Written by the app. source_types table No {} Column types of the template file. Written by the app. source_file text No "" Name of the template file. Written by the app.

The three csv_* keys only affect how CSV source files are read. They have no effect on Excel files, and no effect on how output files are written: the output CSV format comes from Settings.

The three source_* keys let the editor show columns without reloading the template file. Leave them as the app wrote them, or leave them out.

docs.title: csv_encoding values
docs.text:
Value Use it for "utf8-lossy" Default. UTF-8 files. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are replaced with � instead of stopping the run. "utf8" UTF-8 files, failing with invalid utf-8 sequence on any invalid byte. "cp1252" Files saved by Excel as CSV (separator: semicolon) or CSV (comma delimited) on a Western-European Windows: accented letters then read correctly instead of as �. "latin-1" Files encoded in ISO-8859-1.

Other standard encoding names, such as "utf-16", are also accepted.

Presets saved before version 1.4.0

Presets saved by versions before 1.4.0 contain csv_separator = ";", which forces semicolons. Delete that line to let Flash-Excel detect the separator.

Saving from the Presets page

Selecting Save on the Presets page rewrites [meta] with the name and the template information only: description and the three csv_* keys go back to their defaults. Add them again by hand after saving, or keep such presets out of the editor.

docs.title: The [[steps]] tables
docs.text:
Each [[steps]] table is one step. Its action key says which kind of step it is; the other keys are that step's options.

action Options rename_columns mapping select_columns columns drop_columns columns cast_types casts replace_values column, mapping clean_text columns, ops, case fill_nulls columns, strategy, value add_computed_column target, expression filter_rows combine, conditions deduplicate_rows subset, keep sort_rows by, descending reorder_columns columns

Every option, its allowed values and its default are listed in Steps.

The conditions of filter_rows are written as [[steps.conditions]] tables right after their step, or as an inline list:

[[steps]]
action = "filter_rows"
combine = "OR"
conditions = [
  { column = "country", operator = "eq", value = "France" },
  { column = "country", operator = "eq", value = "Belgium" },
]

docs.title: Writing values
docs.text:
• Column names that contain spaces or symbols must be quoted as keys: { "Last Name" = "last_name" }.
  • Text values use double quotes. For an expression that itself contains double quotes, wrap it in single quotes, which TOML reads literally: expression = 'CONCATENER(first_name, " ", last_name)'.
  • Numbers and booleans have no quotes: value = 30000, descending = true. A quoted number is text.
  • TOML has no empty (null) value. A preset cannot replace a value with an empty cell.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
This preset reads an HR export, cleans it and keeps the active employees earning at least 30,000. It is valid as written: it loads without errors and runs on a matching file.

[meta]
name = "Monthly HR report"
description = "Clean the monthly HR export"
csv_encoding = "utf8-lossy"
csv_decimal_comma = false

[[steps]]
action = "rename_columns"
mapping = { "Last Name" = "last_name", "First Name" = "first_name" }

[[steps]]
action = "drop_columns"
columns = ["Internal ID"]

[[steps]]
action = "cast_types"
casts = { salary = "float", hired_on = "date" }

[[steps]]
action = "replace_values"
column = "status"
mapping = { "A" = "Active", "I" = "Inactive" }

[[steps]]
action = "clean_text"
columns = ["last_name", "first_name"]
ops = ["trim", "collapse"]
case = "title"

[[steps]]
action = "fill_nulls"
columns = ["department"]
strategy = "value"
value = "Unknown"

[[steps]]
action = "add_computed_column"
target = "full_name"
expression = 'CONCATENER(first_name, " ", MAJUSCULE(last_name))'

[[steps]]
action = "filter_rows"
combine = "AND"

[[steps.conditions]]
column = "status"
operator = "eq"
value = "Active"

[[steps.conditions]]
column = "salary"
operator = "gte"
value = 30000

[[steps]]
action = "deduplicate_rows"
subset = ["full_name"]
keep = "first"

[[steps]]
action = "sort_rows"
by = ["department", "salary"]
descending = [false, true]

[[steps]]
action = "select_columns"
columns = ["full_name", "department", "salary", "hired_on"]

[[steps]]
action = "reorder_columns"
columns = ["department", "full_name"]

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
Flash-Excel checks a preset file when it lists or runs it. A file that does not follow this format is not run:

  • In the app, it appears in the preset list marked unreadable; hover over the marker to read the reason.
  • From the command line, the run stops before any file is processed, with exit code 1.
Message Meaning The preset file '…' contains invalid TOML syntax. The file is not valid TOML: a missing quote or bracket, a duplicated key. The details give the line. The preset '…' contains configuration errors: followed by a list The TOML is valid, but a value is missing or not allowed. Each line names the location, for example steps > 0 > cast_types > casts > amount; steps are numbered from 0. Preset file not found: '…'. The path given does not lead to a file.

See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open the settings with Settings in the sidebar. Theme, language and CSV changes apply and are saved as soon as you select them. A read-only preset source is saved only when you select Save in its dialog. Close the window with × or Esc.

The settings are stored in app.config.yaml, in %APPDATA%\flash-excel. You can also edit that file by hand: changes are read on the next start. See Data locations.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Setting (in the app) Values Default app.config.yaml key File values Color palette Blue Gray, GitHub, Warm Dark Blue Gray appearance.palette blue-gray, github-dark, warm-dark Mode Dark, Light Dark appearance.mode dark, light

Each palette has a dark and a light variant. The palette cards preview the colours of the selected mode.

The palettes themselves are defined in theme.config.yaml, next to app.config.yaml. A new version of Flash-Excel that changes the palettes replaces this file and keeps your previous copy as theme.config.yaml.bak. If app.config.yaml names a palette that does not exist, Flash-Excel uses Blue Gray.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Setting (in the app) Values Default app.config.yaml key File values Language English, French The language chosen in the installer; English otherwise locale en, fr

The language applies to the whole interface. It also sets the true/false labels written in Excel output files: True/False in English, VRAI/FAUX in French.

Function names of computed columns stay in French whatever the language. See Computed column functions.

docs.title: CSV output
docs.text:
These settings apply to the CSV files Flash-Excel writes, from the window, launchers, scheduled tasks and the command line. They do not change how CSV source files are read: that is set per preset (see Preset file format).

Setting (in the app) Values Default app.config.yaml key File values Column separator Auto, Semicolon ;, Comma ,, Tab Auto csv.separator auto, semicolon, comma, tab Decimal mark Auto, Comma 1,5, Dot 1.5 Auto csv.decimal auto, comma, dot
  • Auto follows your Windows regional settings (the list separator and the decimal symbol) — the same ones Excel reads, so the file opens in columns on a double-click. On a French Windows, that usually means ; and 1,5; on an English (US) Windows, , and 1.5.
  • A comma cannot be both the separator and the decimal mark. When the separator resolves to a comma, decimals are always written with a dot.
  • In app.config.yaml, an unknown value is treated as auto.

See Set the CSV output format.

docs.title: Read-only preset sources
docs.text:
Shared folders whose presets appear next to your local ones. Flash-Excel only reads them. See Use shared preset folders.

Field (in the app) Description app.config.yaml key Label Name shown with the presets from this folder, e.g. Finance. presets.sources[].label Folder path The folder that contains the .toml presets. presets.sources[].path

Both fields are required. Only the .toml files directly in the folder are listed, not those in sub-folders. Selecting Remove source, then Delete, removes the folder from the list; the folder and its presets will not be deleted.

docs.title: Example app.config.yaml
docs.text:
appearance:
  palette: "github-dark"
  mode: "light"

locale: "fr"

csv:
  separator: "semicolon"
  decimal: "comma"

presets:
  sources:
  - label: Finance
    path: \\server\share\flash-excel\presets

docs.title: Settings that are not in this window
docs.text: The output format, destination folder, naming pattern and error choice are set for each run on the Processing page, under Output and On error. They are not saved between sessions. See Run a preset.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Flash-Excel offers 12 kinds of step. Each section below gives the step's name in the app, its action name in a preset file, its options, and how it behaves. For how steps chain together, see Steps and their order. For the file syntax, see Preset file format.

Column names are case-sensitive everywhere. A step that names a column absent at that point of the chain fails, and the file is handled according to the On error choice (see Error handling).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Step (in the app) Action name Main options Rename columns rename_columns mapping Select columns select_columns columns Drop columns drop_columns columns Cast types cast_types casts Replace values replace_values column, mapping Clean text clean_text columns, ops, case Fill empty cells fill_nulls columns, strategy, value Add computed column add_computed_column target, expression Filter rows filter_rows combine, conditions Deduplicate rows deduplicate_rows subset, keep Sort rows sort_rows by, descending Reorder columns reorder_columns columns

In the tables below, list means a TOML array such as ["a", "b"], and table means a TOML table of key = value pairs such as { "old" = "new" }.

docs.title: Rename columns
docs.text:
rename_columns — gives one or more columns a new name. In the app: Column mapping, one rule per column with Source column and New name.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default mapping table (text → text) Yes At least one pair "current name" = "new name" —

Every current name must exist. Later steps see the new names.

[[steps]]
action = "rename_columns"
mapping = { "Last Name" = "last_name", "First Name" = "first_name" }

docs.title: Select columns
docs.text:
select_columns — keeps only the listed columns, in the listed order, and removes all the others. In the app: Columns to keep; columns toggled off are dropped from the output.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default columns list of text Yes At least one existing column — 
[[steps]]
action = "select_columns"
columns = ["id", "name", "amount"]

docs.title: Drop columns
docs.text:
drop_columns — removes the listed columns and keeps all the others. In the app: Columns to remove. Prefer it to Select columns when you only discard a few columns.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default columns list of text Yes At least one existing column — 
[[steps]]
action = "drop_columns"
columns = ["Internal ID", "tmp"]

docs.title: Cast types
docs.text:
cast_types — converts columns to another data type. In the app: Type casting, one rule per column with Column and Type.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default casts table (column → type) Yes At least one pair; type is one of the values below — Type value Name in the app Notes string Text Any value can become text. int Whole number Text must be a whole number (12, not 1.5 or 12 kg). Decimal numbers are truncated. float Decimal number Text must use a dot as decimal mark (1.5, not 1,5). bool Boolean (True/False) Works from numbers (0 is false, other values true). Text cannot be cast to a boolean. date Date Text must be in YYYY-MM-DD form, for example 2024-03-05. datetime Date & time Text must be in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS form, for example 2024-03-05T10:00:00.

A single value that cannot be converted makes the step fail, with a message such as conversion from str to i64 failed in column 'amount' for 1 out of 1 values: ["abc"]. Clean or replace such values in earlier steps.

[[steps]]
action = "cast_types"
casts = { salary = "float", hired_on = "date" }

docs.title: Replace values
docs.text:
replace_values — replaces exact cell values in one column. Values that are not listed stay unchanged. In the app: Replacements, one rule per value with Column, Find and Replace with; rules on the same column are grouped into one step per column.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default column text Yes An existing column — mapping table (value → value) Yes At least one pair "find" = replacement —
  • Matching is on the whole cell, and case-sensitive: "YES" does not match "yes" or "YES please".
  • Replacements can be text, numbers or true / false. The replacement must suit the column's type: replacing a number with text in a numeric column fails. Cast the column to Text first.
  • A replacement cannot be empty (null): a preset file has no way to store it, and saving such a preset fails with holds a value that cannot be saved to TOML.
[[steps]]
action = "replace_values"
column = "status"
mapping = { "A" = "Active", "I" = "Inactive" }

docs.title: Clean text
docs.text:
clean_text — tidies text in one or more columns. In the app: Add clean action, then pick Target columns, Operations and Case conversion. Each clean action is saved as its own step.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default columns list of text Yes At least one existing text column — ops list of text No Any of trim, collapse, accents, special [] case text No none, lower, upper, title none Value Name in the app Effect trim Trim whitespace Removes spaces at the start and end. collapse Collapse spaces Replaces each run of spaces, tabs or line breaks with a single space. accents Remove accents é becomes e, ç becomes c. Characters with no plain-letter equivalent are removed. special Remove special characters Keeps only letters, digits, underscores and whitespace; removes punctuation and symbols. lower lower Lower case. upper UPPER Upper case. title Title First letter of each word in upper case.

The operations always apply in this order, whatever the order of the list: trim, collapse, accents, special, then case. Removing special characters can therefore leave double spaces behind. The columns must hold text: cast a numeric column to Text first, or the step fails with expected String.

[[steps]]
action = "clean_text"
columns = ["last_name", "first_name"]
ops = ["trim", "collapse"]
case = "title"

docs.title: Fill empty cells
docs.text:
fill_nulls — fills empty cells in one or more columns. In the app: Columns to process, then Fill empty cells with and, for a value, Replacement value.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default columns list of text Yes At least one existing column — strategy text No value, forward, backward value value text, number or true/false When strategy = "value" Any value — Strategy Name in the app Effect value A value Puts value in every empty cell. forward Value above Copies the nearest non-empty value above the cell. backward Value below Copies the nearest non-empty value below the cell.

A cell counts as empty when it holds no value at all. A cell containing spaces or an empty text is not empty. With forward, empty cells at the very top stay empty; with backward, those at the very bottom do.

The replacement value typed in the app is text. Filling a numeric column with it turns the whole column into text; in a preset file, write a number without quotes (value = 0) to keep the column numeric.

[[steps]]
action = "fill_nulls"
columns = ["department"]
strategy = "value"
value = "Unknown"

docs.title: Add computed column
docs.text:
add_computed_column — creates a column, or overwrites an existing one, from a formula. In the app: Add computed column, with New column name and an expression built from Columns, Functions and Separators. Each computed column is saved as its own step, and later ones can use earlier ones.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default target text Yes Name of the column to create. An existing name is overwritten. — expression text Yes A formula, see Computed column functions — 
[[steps]]
action = "add_computed_column"
target = "full_name"
expression = 'CONCATENER(first_name, " ", MAJUSCULE(last_name))'

docs.title: Filter rows
docs.text:
filter_rows — keeps only the rows that match conditions and removes the others. In the app: Keep rows matching All conditions or Any condition, then one rule per condition with Column, Operator and Value.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default combine text No AND (all conditions), OR (any condition) AND conditions list of conditions Yes At least one condition —

Each condition has three options:

Option Type Required Allowed values column text Yes An existing column operator text Yes See the operator table below value text, number or true/false Yes The value to compare with Operator In the app Keeps rows where the cell… eq = equals the value neq ≠ differs from the value gt > is greater than the value gte ≥ is greater than or equal to the value lt < is less than the value lte ≤ is less than or equal to the value contains contains contains the value as plain text startswith starts with starts with the value endswith ends with ends with the value
  • Text comparisons are case-sensitive. contains, starts with and ends with treat the value as plain text (C++ matches only C++), and work on any column by reading it as text.
  • On a numeric column, a value typed as text is converted to a number. A value that is not a number makes the step fail with '…' is not a number, but the column holds numbers (…). Enter a numeric value.
  • On a true/false column, the values true, 1 and yes (any case) mean true; any other text means false.
  • Empty cells never match a condition, so rows with an empty cell in a filtered column are removed.
[[steps]]
action = "filter_rows"
combine = "AND"

[[steps.conditions]]
column = "status"
operator = "eq"
value = "Active"

[[steps.conditions]]
column = "salary"
operator = "gte"
value = 30000

docs.title: Deduplicate rows
docs.text:
deduplicate_rows — removes duplicate rows. Two rows are duplicates when all the key columns match. In the app: Deduplication keys and When duplicates are found, keep.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default subset list of text No Existing columns [] (compare all columns) keep text No first, last, none first Value In the app Effect first First row Keeps the first row of each group of duplicates. last Last row Keeps the last row of each group of duplicates. none (file only) Removes every row that has a duplicate, keeping none of them.

The order of the remaining rows is not guaranteed. Add a Sort rows step if the order matters.

[[steps]]
action = "deduplicate_rows"
subset = ["email"]
keep = "first"

docs.title: Sort rows
docs.text:
sort_rows — orders rows by one or more columns. In the app: Sort keys, one rule per column with Column and Direction (Asc or Desc). Keys apply top to bottom: the first is the primary sort.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default by list of text Yes At least one existing column — descending true/false, or a list of them No One value for all keys, or one per key in by order false

When descending is a list, it must have exactly as many entries as by, or the preset is refused with sort_rows descending list length must match 'by' length.

[[steps]]
action = "sort_rows"
by = ["department", "salary"]
descending = [false, true]

docs.title: Reorder columns
docs.text:
reorder_columns — puts the listed columns first, in the listed order. In the app: Column order, where you drag columns into place.

Option Type Required Allowed values Default columns list of text Yes At least one existing column —

Columns not in the list are kept and placed after the listed ones, in their current order.

[[steps]]
action = "reorder_columns"
columns = ["department", "full_name"]

docs.text: Step-by-step instructions for everything you do in Flash-Excel, grouped in the order you meet them. If you have never used Flash-Excel, start with Get started.

Add a computed column Build a new column from an expression such as CONCATENER(...). Filter rows Keep only the rows that match your conditions. docs.title: Create a launcher
docs.text: Save a .cmd file that runs a preset on the same files when you double-click it, without opening Flash-Excel. Use it for a run you repeat on demand rather than on a schedule.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• On the Processing page, the files to process are loaded and the preset is selected. See Load source files.
  • The preset and the source files stay where they are: the launcher uses their current paths.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. On the Processing page, under Scheduled and manual execution, select Configure execution. The Schedule or create a launcher window opens.
  2. Check the Execution name, the Input files and the output settings: Destination folder, Format and Naming pattern.
  3. Select Create a .cmd launcher.
  4. In the save dialog, choose where to save the launcher. Its name defaults to the Execution name, with the .cmd extension. Keep that extension.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Launcher created. Double-click it to run this configuration. appears, and the window shows where the launcher was saved.

Double-click the launcher to run it. A console window opens, shows one line per file, either <file> -> <output path> (<n> rows) or <file> FAILED: <reason>, and stays open until you press a key. If a file fails, the launcher goes on with the next one.

To remove a launcher, delete its .cmd file.

Names and paths that are refused

The Execution name must have 1 to 200 characters, without \ / : * ? " < > | % !. The paths of the preset, the files and the destination folder cannot contain %, ! or quotes.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Schedule a preset to run the same configuration every day.
  • Run from the command line

docs.title: Disable or delete a scheduled task
docs.text: Stop a preset that Flash-Excel scheduled from running every day, for a while or for good.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A task created with Add to Task Scheduler. See Schedule a preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the Windows Start menu, search for Task Scheduler and open it.
  2. In the left pane, expand Task Scheduler Library and open the Flash-Excel folder.
  3. Right-click the task, then:
    • choose Disable to pause future runs, or
    • choose Delete and confirm to remove the task.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
A disabled task stays in the list with the status Disabled and does not run until you choose Enable. A deleted task is gone from the list.

Disabling or deleting a task does not delete your preset, your source files or the files already produced.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Schedule a preset to create a new task.
  • Create a launcher to run the same configuration on demand instead.

docs.title: Run from the command line
docs.text: Run a preset on one or more files from a command prompt or a script, without opening the Flash-Excel window. This is what scheduled tasks and launchers do behind the scenes, and you can use it in your own batch files.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Flash-Excel installed. See Get started.
  • The path of the Flash-Excel executable. To find it, open Configure execution on the Processing page: the window shows Uses the installed application: followed by the path.
  • A preset file. Your presets are in Documents\flash-excel\presets, one .toml file per preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Open a Command Prompt or a PowerShell window.

  2. Run the Flash-Excel executable with --preset and --input. Replace the paths with yours:

    Command PromptPowerShell 
    "<path to>\Flash-Excel.exe" --preset "%USERPROFILE%\Documents\flash-excel\presets\monthly_report.toml" --input "C:\Data\january.xlsx" "C:\Data\february.xlsx" --output "C:\Data\clean"

    & "<path to>\Flash-Excel.exe" --preset "$HOME\Documents\flash-excel\presets\monthly_report.toml" --input "C:\Data\january.xlsx" "C:\Data\february.xlsx" --output "C:\Data\clean"

  3. Add options if needed:

    Option Effect Default --output <folder> Destination folder. A relative folder is created inside the default one. Documents\flash-excel\output --format <format> keep (same as source), xlsx, csv or parquet. keep --pattern <text> Output file name without extension; {name} is the source file name. {name}_clean --debug Writes more detail to the log file. Off

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
Each file is processed on its own, and the window prints one line per file:

january.xlsx -> C:\Data\clean\january_clean.xlsx (1250 rows)
february.xlsx FAILED: <reason>

A failing file does not stop the others. When the command ends, its exit code tells a script what happened:

Exit code Meaning 0 Every file succeeded. 1 At least one file failed. 2 The command-line arguments are wrong.

The same lines are written to the Flash-Excel log file. See Data locations.

Wait for the run in an interactive prompt

Flash-Excel is a windowed application. Typed directly at an interactive Command Prompt, the prompt can come back before the run ends, with the result lines printed after it, and %ERRORLEVEL% is then not the run's exit code. To wait for the end and read the exit code, run the command from a batch file (.cmd), as launchers do.

Same settings as the app

A command-line run uses the CSV output settings chosen in Settings › CSV output. See Set the CSV output format.

Let Flash-Excel write the command

Schedule a preset and Create a launcher build this command for you from the Processing page.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Command line — the full option reference.
  • Schedule a preset

docs.title: Schedule a preset
docs.text: Run a preset on the same files every day at a set time, without opening Flash-Excel. Flash-Excel creates the task for you in the Windows Task Scheduler.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• On the Processing page, the files to process are loaded and the preset is selected. See Load source files and Run a preset.
  • The preset and the source files stay where they are: the task uses their current paths.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. On the Processing page, under Scheduled and manual execution, select Configure execution. The Schedule or create a launcher window opens.
  2. Check the settings:
    • Execution name: the name of the task. It defaults to flash-excel followed by the preset file name.
    • Daily time (scheduled task): the time of the daily run. It defaults to 08:00.
    • Preset and Input files: the preset and the files the task will process.
    • Destination folder, Format and Naming pattern: the output of the task. They start with the values of the Processing page; select Choose an output folder to pick another folder.
  3. Select Add to Task Scheduler.
  4. In the Confirm scheduled task creation window, read the summary and the warning, then select Confirm creation.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Scheduled task “” created. appears. The task is in the Windows Task Scheduler, under Task Scheduler Library › Flash-Excel, and runs every day at the time you set.

  • The task runs while your Windows session is open. Flash-Excel itself can be closed.
  • If a file fails, the task goes on with the next file. The On error choice of the Processing page does not apply.
  • Each run replaces the output files of the previous run when the names are the same.

You are responsible for the task

The task repeats every day until you disable or delete it. Check the files, the preset and the destination before you confirm.

Names and paths that are refused

The Execution name must have 1 to 200 characters, without \ / : * ? " < > | % !. The paths of the preset, the files and the destination folder cannot contain %, ! or quotes.

Copy the command instead

Advanced: copy the scheduling command copies a schtasks command to the clipboard, to create the task yourself. Windows refuses this command when it is longer than 261 characters; use Add to Task Scheduler in that case.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:

  • Run from the command line — what the task actually runs.
  • Disable or delete a scheduled task
  • The scheduled task did not run

docs.title: Load source files
docs.text: Load the Excel or CSV files you want to transform on the Processing page. You can load one file or a whole batch that a preset processes one after the other.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Files in a supported format: .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .csv. See File formats.
  • For a batch, files with the same column layout: the step lists are built from the first file only.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
Pick the filesDrag and drop
  1. In the sidebar, select Processing.
  2. Click the drop zone Drop your Excel/CSV files here — or click to browse.
  3. In the file dialog, select one file, or several with Ctrl or Shift, then confirm.
  1. In the sidebar, select Processing.
  2. Drag one or several files from the Windows Explorer and drop them onto the window.

Files Flash-Excel cannot read are left out of the list.

To replace the list, select Load file above the list and pick other files: the new selection replaces the previous one. To empty the list, select Clear. Both are unavailable while a run is in progress.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
Under Input file, each file appears as a row with its name, size and the status Pending. The header shows the number of files, for example 3 file(s), and the first row also shows its number of columns.

How Flash-Excel reads the files

Only the first sheet of an Excel workbook is read. For a CSV file, the column separator is detected automatically, unless the preset file sets one (see Preset file).

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Preview a transformation
  • Run a preset
  • If a file is refused, see Unsupported file format; if a CSV loads as one column, see A CSV source loads as a single column.

docs.title: Add a computed column
docs.text: Add a column whose values are calculated from other columns, for example a full name built from a first name and a last name, or a price rounded to two decimals.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A preset open on the Presets page, with a template file loaded. See Create a preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Under Action configuration, select Add computed column.
  2. In the panel, select Add computed column. The New computed column window opens.
  3. In New column name, type the name of the column to create.
  4. Build the formula in Expression:
    • select a column under Columns to insert it;
    • select a separator under Separators to insert it as text, for example " ";
    • under Functions, pick a category (Text, Math, Date or Logic), then select a function to insert it. Hover a function to see its description and an Example.
  5. Check the expression, then select Save.
  6. Repeat from step 2 for each column to add, then select Save in the toolbar to save the preset.

Examples of expressions:

Expression Result CONCATENER(first_name, " ", last_name) Joins the two columns with a space. MAJUSCULE(last_name) The last name in upper case. ARRONDI(price, 2) The price rounded to two decimal places. ANNEE(birth_date) The year of a date column. SI(age >= 18, "adult", "minor") adult when the condition holds, minor otherwise.

Column names with spaces or symbols

Write a column whose name contains spaces, starts with a digit or holds symbols between square brackets, for example [Order date]. Selecting the column under Columns inserts it in the right form.

Function names are in French

The function names (CONCATENER, MAJUSCULE, SI…) follow French Excel and stay the same whatever the interface language. Text values go between double quotes.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text: The computed column is listed in the panel with its expression. Select the pencil icon to edit it, or the bin icon to delete it. In the following steps, such as Filter rows or Sort rows, the new column is available like any other.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Computed-column functions — every function, its arguments and examples.
  • Preview a transformation to check the values.

docs.title: Add steps to a preset
docs.text: Add the transformations a preset applies: renaming, selecting or dropping columns, converting types, cleaning text, filtering, sorting and more. Each action has its own panel in the editor, and Flash-Excel runs the actions in a fixed order.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A preset open on the Presets page. See Create a preset.
  • A template file loaded under Load the Excel template, so that the steps can list the columns. Without it, the hint Load a file to enable column mapping is shown.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Presets, then select the preset in the list on the left.
  2. Under Action configuration, select an action in the list, for example Filter rows. Hover the i icon next to an action to read what it does.
  3. Configure the action in the panel on the right. Most actions start with Add a rule; the panel header shows how many rules are configured.
  4. Repeat for every action you need. An action with at least one rule shows its count in the list.
  5. Select Save.

The twelve actions, in the order Flash-Excel runs them:

Order Action What it does 1 Rename columns Give one or more columns a new name. 2 Select columns Keep only the columns you choose. 3 Drop columns Remove the columns you choose. 4 Cast types Convert columns to a target data type. 5 Replace values Find and replace values inside columns. 6 Clean text Trim, normalise and strip whitespace. 7 Fill empty cells Replace null values using a strategy. 8 Add computed column Create a new column from an expression. 9 Filter rows Keep only rows matching your conditions. 10 Deduplicate rows Remove duplicate rows by key columns. 11 Sort rows Order rows by one or more columns. 12 Reorder columns Change the column order.

The column lists of each action show the columns as they are at that point of the run, and renaming a column updates the later actions that use it. See Steps and order.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Preset saved appears and the step count of the preset is updated in the list. If a step is incomplete, the message Preset saved, but these steps were refused and are not in the file: … names it: complete it and save again.

Changing the order of the steps

You cannot move a step in the editor: the Presets page always saves the actions in the order of the table above. See Steps and order.

Column order in the output

To change the order of the columns in the output file, use the Reorder columns action.

Loading a template with different columns

If you load a template file whose columns differ from those saved in the preset, the Column layout changed dialog lists the Columns no longer in file and the New columns in file. Select Load & clean up references to remove the missing columns from the steps, Ignore differences to keep the steps as they are, or Cancel.

docs.title: Create a preset
docs.text: Create a preset when you have a new kind of file to transform. A preset holds the steps to apply and remembers the columns of a template file, so you can edit it later without that file.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A template file: an Excel or CSV file with the same columns as the files you will process (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .csv).

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Presets.
  2. Next to Presets, select the + button (New preset). A new preset named Preset 1 (or the next free number) opens in the editor.
  3. In the name field of the toolbar, replace the default name with a name of your own.
  4. Under Load the Excel template, select Load a file and pick your template file.
  5. Under Action configuration, add at least one step. See Add steps to a preset.
  6. Select Save.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Preset saved appears, and the preset is listed on the left with the label Local and its number of steps. It is also offered in the Preset list of the Processing page.

The preset is saved as a .toml file in Documents\flash-excel\presets. The file name comes from the preset name: Monthly report becomes monthly_report.toml.

A new preset is not saved until you select Save

Until then, it exists only in the editor and is not listed.

Renaming a preset

To rename a preset, select it, change its name and select Save: its file is renamed too. If another preset already uses the same file name, Flash-Excel refuses the save and asks you to choose another name.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Add steps to a preset
  • Preview a transformation
  • Presets — what a preset contains.
  • Preset file — the format of the .toml file.

docs.title: Delete a preset
docs.text: Remove a preset you no longer need. Deleting a preset removes its file from your presets folder.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A preset of your own, listed with the label Local. Presets from a shared folder cannot be deleted from Flash-Excel.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Presets.
  2. Select the preset in the list on the left.
  3. In the toolbar, select Delete.
  4. In the Delete preset dialog, check the name after Are you sure you want to delete, then select Delete.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Preset deleted appears and the preset leaves the list. Its .toml file is deleted from Documents\flash-excel\presets.

This action cannot be undone

Flash-Excel keeps no copy of a deleted preset. Export the preset first if you may need it again.

Scheduled tasks and launchers

A scheduled task or a launcher that uses the deleted preset fails on its next run. Remove it too: see Schedule a preset.

docs.title: Export a preset
docs.text: Save a copy of a preset file anywhere you choose, to back it up, send it to a colleague or place it in a shared folder.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A saved preset of your own, listed with the label Local. Presets from a shared folder cannot be exported.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Presets.
  2. Select the preset in the list on the left.
  3. In the toolbar, select Export.
  4. In the save dialog, choose a folder. The file keeps the name of the preset file, for example monthly_report.toml; change it if needed.
  5. Select Save in the dialog.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The message Preset exported appears and a copy of the .toml file is in the folder you chose. The preset in Flash-Excel is unchanged.

To use the copy on another computer, put it in the Documents\flash-excel\presets folder of that computer, or in a folder added as a shared source.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:

  • Data locations — where Flash-Excel stores presets.

docs.title: Filter rows
docs.text: Keep only the rows that match your conditions, for example the active customers or the orders above an amount. The other rows are left out of the output file.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A preset open on the Presets page, with a template file loaded. See Create a preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Under Action configuration, select Filter rows.
  2. Next to Keep rows matching, choose how the conditions combine:
    • All conditions: a row is kept when it matches every condition;
    • Any condition: a row is kept when it matches at least one condition.
  3. Select Add a rule. A condition row appears.
  4. In the condition row:
    1. pick the column;
    2. pick the operator: =, ≠, >, ≥, <, ≤, contains, starts with or ends with;
    3. type the value to compare with in Value.
  5. Repeat steps 3 and 4 for each condition. Select × at the end of a row to remove it.
  6. Select Save.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The Filter rows action shows the number of conditions in the list of actions. When the preset runs, only the matching rows are written.

How values are compared

  • On a numeric column, type a number: a text value on a numeric column makes the run fail with an error.
  • contains, starts with and ends with compare the text exactly as typed, including upper and lower case.
  • A condition with an empty value is ignored. With no condition at all, every row is kept.

Check the filter on a preview

The preview reads only the first 100 rows of the file. If no row of that sample matches, the preview says so even though later rows may match. See Preview a transformation.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Steps — the Filter rows options in detail.
  • A step cannot find a column if a run fails on a filter.

docs.title: Use shared preset folders
docs.text: Use presets stored in a shared folder, for example a team folder on a network drive, alongside your own presets. Flash-Excel reads these presets but never changes them.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A folder that contains preset files (.toml) and that you can open from your computer.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Settings.
  2. Under Read-only preset sources, select Add source.
  3. In Label, type a short name that identifies the folder, for example Finance.
  4. In Folder path, type the path of the folder, or select the folder icon (Browse for a folder) to pick it.
  5. Select Save.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The folder is listed under Read-only preset sources. Its presets appear with the label you typed instead of Local: in the Preset list of the Processing page the next time you open that page, and on the Presets page after you restart Flash-Excel.

You can open, preview and run a shared preset like your own. Save and Delete are unavailable for it, because shared folders are read-only in Flash-Excel.

To change a source, select Edit next to it. To remove it from the list, select the Remove source icon, then Delete in the Remove shared source? dialog. The folder and its presets are not deleted.

Folder not available

If a shared folder cannot be reached when Flash-Excel lists the presets, for example when the network drive is disconnected, its presets are simply not listed. They come back once the folder is reachable again.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Export a preset to place one of your presets in a shared folder.
  • Settings — every setting and where it is stored.

docs.title: Preview a transformation
docs.text: Check what a preset does to your data before writing any file. The preview applies the preset to the first 100 rows of a source file and shows the result in a table.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• At least one source file loaded on the Processing page. See Load source files.
  • A saved preset. Changes made on the Presets page are previewed only once you select Save there.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Processing.
  2. Under Preset, select the preset to check.
  3. Select Preview.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The Transformation preview window opens. It shows the columns and rows after the transformation, and the number of rows left, for example 87 rows after transformation. Empty cells read null. No output file is written.

Close the window with ×, Esc, or by clicking outside it.

What the preview covers

  • Only the first file of the list is previewed, even when several files are loaded.
  • Only the first 100 rows of that file are read. Filter rows, Deduplicate rows and Sort rows therefore act on this sample only: a row beyond the first 100 can still match your filters in a real run.
  • If no row of the sample is left, the window says No rows remain in this sample after transformation.

If the preview fails, the window shows Preview failed: followed by the reason. Look the reason up in Troubleshooting. If the preview ignores your last edits, see Changes to a preset are not used by the run.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Run a preset
  • Add steps to a preset to adjust the preset.

docs.title: Run a preset
docs.text: Apply a preset to one or several source files and write the transformed files. You choose the output format, the destination folder, the file names, and what happens when a file fails.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• At least one source file loaded on the Processing page. See Load source files.
  • A saved preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Processing.
  2. Under Preset, select the preset. Each entry shows the preset name, its source (Local or the label of a shared folder) and its number of actions. The box below lists the actions of the selected preset.

  3. Under Output, set the output:

    Field What to enter Default Format Same as source, .xlsx (Excel), .csv (UTF-8) or .parquet. Same as source Destination folder The folder where the files are written. Type a path, or select the folder icon to pick one. Documents\flash-excel\output Naming pattern The output file name, without extension. {name} stands for the name of the source file. {name}_clean

  4. Under On error, choose what happens when a file fails:

    • Skip file (continue queue): the failing file is not written and the run goes on with the next file;
    • Stop all (halt on first error): the run stops at the first failing file;
    • Ignore (write partial): the failing step is skipped, the other steps still apply and the file is written.
  5. Select Run preset.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The files are processed one after the other. Each row shows its progress and its status: Pending, Running, Done, Error or Skipped. At the bottom of the panel, Progress covers the whole batch, with the counters Rows out, Errors, Warnings and Elapsed.

The Console logs each step with its row counts, then a line such as Done in 0.42s → <output path> for each written file. Use the All, Info, Step, Warn and Err filters to narrow the log.

With the default settings, C:\Data\sales.xlsx gives Documents\flash-excel\output\sales_clean.xlsx.

Existing files are replaced

A file with the same name in the destination folder is overwritten. Change the Naming pattern or the Destination folder to keep earlier results.

Same as source with .xls and .xlsm files

Same as source writes only .xlsx and .csv files. For an .xls or .xlsm source, choose .xlsx (Excel) as the Format, or the file fails with Unsupported format: 'xls'.

Relative folder

A relative Destination folder, such as monthly, is created inside Documents\flash-excel\output.

If a file ends with Error, read its message in the Console and look it up in Troubleshooting: a missing column is covered in A step cannot find a column, a locked file in Permission denied.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:

  • Error handling — the three error modes in detail.
  • Set the CSV output format

docs.title: Stop a run
docs.text: Interrupt a run in progress, for example when you notice the wrong preset or the wrong files.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • A run in progress on the Processing page. See Run a preset.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text: 1. On the Processing page, select the square stop button to the right of Run preset. It is available only while a run is in progress.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
Flash-Excel lets the current step finish, then stops before the next step or the next file. The Console shows Run stopped by user.

  • Files already marked Done are written and stay in the destination folder.
  • The file being processed is not written if steps were still left to apply, and is marked Skipped.
  • Files not reached yet are marked Skipped.

To process the remaining files, select Load file, pick only those files, then select Run preset. See Load source files.

docs.text:
• Run a preset
  • Error handling

docs.title: Change the language
docs.text: Switch the Flash-Excel interface between English and French.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • None.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Settings.
  2. Under Language, select English or French.
  3. Close the Settings window.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The interface switches to the chosen language at once, and Flash-Excel keeps it the next time it starts.

Language chosen in the installer

When you install Flash-Excel, the language picked in the installer becomes the interface language. A later choice in Settings wins, until you reinstall.

What the language also changes

The language also sets how true/false (Boolean) values are written in Excel output: True / False in English, VRAI / FAUX in French. The names of the computed-column functions, such as CONCATENER, stay in French in both languages.

docs.title: Change the theme
docs.text: Change the colors of the Flash-Excel window: pick a color palette and a dark or light mode.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • None.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Settings.
  2. Under Appearance › Color palette, select a palette: Blue Gray, GitHub or Warm Dark.
  3. Under Mode, select Dark or Light.
  4. Close the Settings window with ×, Esc, or by clicking outside it.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text: The window takes the new colors as soon as you select them, and Flash-Excel keeps them the next time it starts. By default, Flash-Excel uses the Blue Gray palette in Dark mode.

docs.title: Set the CSV output format
docs.text: Choose the column separator and the decimal mark of the CSV files Flash-Excel writes, for example to match the program that reads them.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • None. The setting applies to every CSV file Flash-Excel writes: runs from the Processing page, scheduled tasks, launchers and command-line runs.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, select Settings.
  2. Under CSV output › Column separator, select Auto, Semicolon ;, Comma , or Tab.
  3. Under Decimal mark, select Auto, Comma 1,5 or Dot 1.5.
  4. Close the Settings window.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The next CSV files written use the chosen separator and decimal mark. Files written before are not changed.

Auto, the default for both settings, follows your Windows regional settings — the same ones Excel reads, so the file opens in columns on a double-click. Choose a fixed value when another program, or a computer with other regional settings, reads the files.

Comma separator and comma decimals

With Comma , as the separator, decimal numbers are always written with a dot, even if Decimal mark is set to Comma 1,5: a comma in the numbers would split them across two columns.

docs.title: Update Flash-Excel
docs.text: Install a new version of Flash-Excel from inside the application, without downloading an installer again.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Flash-Excel installed with the installer. See Get started.
  • An internet connection when Flash-Excel starts.
  • No run in progress: Flash-Excel closes during the update.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Start Flash-Excel. It checks for a new version when it opens.
  2. When a new version exists, a link Update to v appears at the bottom right of the window, next to the current version number. Select it.
  3. The link reads Updating… while the new version downloads. Flash-Excel then closes to install it.
  4. Start Flash-Excel again if it does not reopen by itself.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The version number at the bottom right of the window shows the new version.

Your presets, settings and output files are kept: they are stored outside the installation folder. See Data locations.

No update link

Without a link, you already have the latest version, or the check could not reach the update server. You can also install a new version by running its installer from the Releases page.
